citation: U.S. Geological Survey. 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1-metre bare-earth digital elevation model, Cook County, Illinois (lidar acquired 3 June 2017), read through the USGS Elevation Point Query Service.
author: U.S. Geological Survey
locator: point queries recorded one per reading in data/terrain/e1871_grade_readings.json (each row carries its query URL); values in feet, NAVD88
rights_note: A U.S. Government work; public domain.
access_notes: The point service answered 200 to every query on 2026-09-28; each reading records the acquisition date and the 1 m resolution the service reported.
note: MODERN measurement, not historical evidence. Read by T-1251 for the ground's elevation at named points of the 1904 Prairie Avenue reach, and carried back to 1904 only as the terrain spec argues it: inferred where houses of the period still stand at their own grade in front of the reading, reconstructed elsewhere (docs/RESEARCH/terrain_e1871_postfire.md zones 3 and 4). Cross-checked against City of Chicago benchmark 289 (chicago_elevation_benchmarks), which it matches to 0.00 ft under the Chicago City Datum conversion the terrain dossier quotes.
what_it_supplies: The modern bare-earth elevation, to the nearest hundredth of a foot, at any point queried
what_it_does_not_supply: Any elevation as of 1904 on its own authority
Where the ground has been re-graded since, which only a standing building of the period can witness
